page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-180-lssd is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. The system delivers 180 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 90 physical cores with dual threading enabled. It is configured with 1440 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage comprises 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across 16 bundled solid-state disks. The configuration does not include discrete GPUs.

Hardware benchmark metrics show leading parallel computation and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieved 277,236.34 on stress-ng multi-core testing and 22,262.0 on Geekbench multi-core evaluation. Memory performance is characterized by 13,557.95 GB/sec cached small-block read speeds and 176.26 GB/sec large-block write throughput. Compute workloads benefit from AVX-512 vector extensions, including VNNI and bfloat16 instruction sets, alongside hardware-accelerated VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. Redis SET transaction rates reached 212.07 million operations per second, confirming high data ingestion rates.

Consolidation into a large 180-vCPU single-node deployment delivers significant compute and memory density, though single-core benchmark metrics place in the upper-quartile rather than peak tiers. The architectural focus centers on throughput scaling across large core counts and high RAM capacity rather than single-threaded acceleration.

Configured with extensive memory capacity, 180 threads of execution, and 6.4 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, the c3d-highmem-180-lssd is aligned with in-memory database engines, distributed caching clusters, large-scale ETL data transformation, and multi-threaded analytical processing workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-180-lssd is a memory-optimized compute instance driven by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 180 dedicated vCPUs derived from 90 physical cores, 1440 GB of system RAM, and 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage spread across 16 drives, without discrete GPU acceleration. The hardware delivers top-tier parallel compute capability, reaching 277,236.34 in stress-ng multi-core execution and 212.07 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Supported by AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and bfloat16, the system handles heavy vector computation and data manipulation efficiently. While single-threaded performance lands in the upper-quartile range, the balance of memory density, core parallelism, and fast local NVMe storage fits large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caches, and analytical processing engines.
